summary: Polk County tower on Little Frog Mountain, Cherokee NF; 1929 Forest Service road and planned seasonal staffing; Landforms marks it removed.

facts.status_note: Tennessee Landforms lists the tower as removed; no removal date found.

access.note: Forest Service land in the Cherokee National Forest. No source describes the tower site itself today.

visit.trail_note: Accessible by a series of trails and by the Kimsey Mountain Highway, a Forest Service road (Wikipedia).

events.note: Forest Service built a three-quarter-mile road from the Kimsey Highway to the tower. The road was meant to let the lookout man drive up to it, which suggests the tower was already in use.
Planned seasonal staffing: the lookout man would be stationed at the tower during dry periods. The article describes a plan, not a staffing record.
Tennessee Landforms waypoint POT002 is marked removed. No removal year given.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1929 Cherokee Scout item calls the tower Sassafras Knob Lookout Tower; Tennessee Landforms calls the waypoint Little Frog. Both sit on Little Frog Mountain in Polk County, so they probably name one tower, but no source links the two names directly. The story uses both.

notes_for_editor: The name link is an inference. The 1929 article calls the tower Sassafras Knob Lookout Tower on Little Frog Mountain; Landforms has a Little Frog waypoint at 3,322 ft in Polk County, which matches the mountain's height. No source reviewed ties the two names together directly. Staffing is the 1929 plan from the newspaper, not a record of staffing. The Landforms code 'cnf' is not explained on its page, so it is not interpreted. No build year, removal year or current site condition appears in any source read. The Facebook Polk County history page showing 'Sassafras Tower on Little Frog Mountain' appeared in search but was not read, so it is not cited.
